westminster.name: Westminster
westminster.description: The political and royal heart of London, Westminster combines world-famous landmarks with elegant residential enclaves. From the grandeur of Belgravia to the village feel of Marylebone, it attracts diplomats, policy professionals, and finance executives who demand centrality and prestige.
westminster.demographic: MPs, policy advisors, diplomats, finance executives, established professionals aged 30–55

camden.name: Camden
camden.description: Camden is London's creative powerhouse — a vibrant mix of alternative culture, tech innovation, and beautiful residential streets. From the iconic Camden Market to the leafy heights of Hampstead and the intellectual buzz of Bloomsbury, it's the borough of choice for creatives, tech founders, and media professionals.
camden.demographic: Creatives, tech entrepreneurs, academics, media professionals, musicians, ages 22–45

kensington-chelsea.name: Kensington & Chelsea
kensington-chelsea.description: The Royal Borough of Kensington and Chelsea represents the pinnacle of prime central London living. White stucco terraces, garden squares, and world-class museums define this affluent enclave. Home to international diplomats, private equity partners, and established families seeking exceptional schools and discreet luxury.
kensington-chelsea.demographic: High-net-worth international families, diplomats, private equity, entrepreneurs, ages 35–60

tower-hamlets.name: Tower Hamlets
tower-hamlets.description: Tower Hamlets is London's fastest-transforming borough, anchored by the Canary Wharf financial district and stretching to vibrant East End neighbourhoods. From slick riverside towers to converted warehouses in Shoreditch and Bethnal Green, it offers a compelling mix of urban energy, green space, and relative value.
tower-hamlets.demographic: Finance professionals, tech workers, young families, university staff, ages 24–40

wandsworth.name: Wandsworth
wandsworth.description: Wandsworth is south-west London's family powerhouse — combining excellent state schools, vast green spaces, and some of the lowest council tax in the capital. Battersea's Power Station regeneration has brought riverside luxury, while Clapham Junction remains one of Britain's busiest transport hubs. Popular with young families priced out of Fulham and Chelsea.
wandsworth.demographic: Young families, City professionals, private equity, established couples aged 28–45

hackney.name: Hackney
hackney.description: Hackney is east London's creative and cultural epicentre. From the independent cafes and galleries of London Fields to the nightlife of Dalston and the canal-side calm of Hackney Wick, it's the borough of choice for artists, designers, and tech workers. Rapidly gentrifying but retaining its authentic edge — one of London's most exciting property markets.
hackney.demographic: Artists, designers, tech founders, musicians, young professionals aged 24–38

islington.name: Islington
islington.description: Islington blends Georgian elegance with modern energy — Upper Street's restaurants and boutiques draw crowds from across London, while the quiet squares of Barnsbury and Canonbury offer village-like calm minutes from King's Cross. A favourite for barristers, academics, and media executives who want Zone 1 proximity without Westminster's formality.
islington.demographic: Barristers, academics, media executives, politicians, established professionals aged 30–50

southwark.name: Southwark
southwark.description: Southwark spans the South Bank's cultural institutions, the gastronomic mecca of Borough Market, and the leafy residential streets of Dulwich. Home to the Shard, Tate Modern, and Shakespeare's Globe — it's where London's history meets its skyline. Strong demand from culture-sector professionals, NHS staff at Guy's & St Thomas', and City workers seeking a short commute.
southwark.demographic: Culture professionals, NHS staff, City workers, creatives, young families aged 26–42
